model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for five different model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 in linear scale with major tick marks every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 in linear scale with major tick marks every 0.1 unit. All five lines begin near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep initial decline before gradually flattening as iterations increase. The “Vanilla” model (purple solid line) consistently shows the lowest loss across the entire range, ending near 2.48 at 140,000 iterations. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” model (blue solid line) starts slightly higher than Vanilla and ends near 2.62. The “SepLLM (n=64, H)” model (orange solid line) begins near 3.3 and ends near 2.54. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” model (red solid line) follows closely behind, ending near 2.52. The “SepLLM (n=128)” model (dark blue solid line) starts near 3.3 and ends near 2.50, showing slightly better convergence than the n=64 variants but still higher than Vanilla. All lines show smooth, monotonic decreases with no visible oscillations or plateaus.
